newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan earthquake toll rises to at least 35.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan earthquake toll rises to at least 35.

text.p: At least 35 people were killed when Pakistan's southwestern province of Baluchistan was hit by a violent earthquake on Friday, local officials said.

They said 29 people had been killed in the town of Harnai, about 100 km (65 miles) southeast of the provincial capital of Quetta. Three people were killed in Quetta itself and at least three died in the town of Sibi to the southeast.
Zarar Haider, deputy commissioner in Sibi, told Reuters by telephone that troops had been sent to Harnai to help in rescue operations. "We are sending help by rail and by helicopter," he added.

A government seismic centre in the northwestern town of Peshawar measured the earthquake at 6.0 on the Richter scale. It placed the epicentre in the Koh-i-Suleman mountain range, north of Quetta, near the Afghan border.
The U.S. Geological Survey's National Earthquake Information Centre in Golden, Colorado, measured the earthquake at 7.3 on the Richter scale.

Frank Baldwin, a physical science technician at the centre, said the earthquake occurred at 2108 GMT and was centred 70 miles (110 km) east southeast of Quetta, or 395 miles (630 km) southwest of Islamabad.
